# AUDIT.md format

`_m365/AUDIT.md` is generated by `scripts/audit_checks.py report`. Its first line is
`# AUDIT`; the first fenced `json` block after it is the machine-readable summary that
the local tooling parses. Prose sections follow.

````markdown
# AUDIT

```json
{
  "schema": "m365-audit/1",
  "task": "<slug>",
  "verdict": "PASS",
  "final_round": 2,
  "max_rounds": 3,
  "rounds": [
    {
      "round": 1,
      "verdict": "FAIL",
      "checks": [
        { "id": "syntax", "status": "PASS" },
        { "id": "json", "status": "PASS" },
        { "id": "scope", "status": "PASS" },
        { "id": "forbidden", "status": "FAIL", "detail": "src/app.py:12: print\\(" },
        { "id": "files", "status": "PASS", "detail": "2 changed" },
        { "id": "AC-1", "status": "PASS" },
        { "id": "AC-2", "status": "FAIL", "detail": "tests/test_app.py has no empty-name case" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

## Round 1

| Check | Status | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| syntax | PASS | |
| forbidden | FAIL | src/app.py:12: print\( |
| AC-2 | FAIL | tests/test_app.py has no empty-name case |

Notes: ...
````

Rules:

- `verdict` at the top is the verdict of the latest round. `final_round` is that round's
  number.
- Check ids `syntax`, `json`, `scope`, `forbidden`, `files` are deterministic; `AC-n`
  are judgements. `forbidden` covers every line of each added or modified text file,
  not only the lines the change introduced. `status` is `PASS` or `FAIL`. A FAIL
  carries a `detail` naming the file and line where possible.
- Earlier rounds are preserved when a new round is reported.
